name: Parga
title: Holidays in Parga
intro: A colourful mainland Greek town tumbling down to a bay of islets, with a Venetian castle above and sandy beaches all around. Here's what Parga is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Parga's colourful houses rising above the harbour
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: June and September are best, with a warm sea and fewer crowds. July and August are hot and busy. The season runs from May to October, and most hotels close in winter.

things.name: Venetian castle
things.blurb: Climb to the ruined castle for the view over the town and islets.

things.name: Valtos beach
things.blurb: A long sandy beach over the hill, or by water taxi.

things.name: Lichnos beach
things.blurb: A sheltered bay with sea caves you can visit by boat.

things.name: Acheron river
things.blurb: Wade up the cold, clear river through a gorge, said to be the gateway to Hades.

things.name: Paxos and Antipaxos
things.blurb: Boat trips to the islands' turquoise coves.

things.name: Waterfront tavernas
things.blurb: Grilled fish and meze looking out at the island chapel.

faqs.question: Is Parga worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of the prettiest towns on the Greek mainland, with island-style beaches but easier to reach than many islands.

faqs.question: How do you get to Parga?
faqs.answer: Fly into Preveza, about an hour's drive away, which has summer flights from the UK. Corfu is another option, with a ferry and drive.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Parga?
faqs.answer: June and September, around 27 to 28°C with a warm sea.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need in Parga?
faqs.answer: A week gives time for the beaches, a boat trip to Paxos and the Acheron river.

faqs.question: Is Parga good for families?
faqs.answer: Yes. The beaches are sandy and calm, and boat taxis make getting around easy.
